Package com.nexuslink.protocol.snmp

Class UsmPrivacy

java.lang.Object
com.nexuslink.protocol.snmp.UsmPrivacy
public final class UsmPrivacy extends Object
The privacy (encryption) half of the SNMPv3 User-based Security Model, complementing the auth-only UsmSecurity. It implements the two classic USM privacy protocols using nothing but the JDK javax.crypto stack, so — like UsmSecurity — every operation is pure, deterministic and fully unit-testable offline:
  • DES-CBC (RFC 3414 §8). The auth-localized key supplies both halves of the DES material: bytes 0–7 are the DES key and bytes 8–15 are the pre-IV. The 8-octet salt (engine boots ‖ a local integer) travels in msgPrivacyParameters; the actual CBC IV is pre-IV XOR salt. Plaintext is padded up to a multiple of the 8-octet block and encrypted with DES/CBC/NoPadding.
  • AES-128-CFB (RFC 3826). The first 16 octets of the localized key are the AES key. The 128-bit IV is engineBoots(4) || engineTime(4) || salt(8), where the 64-bit salt is what travels in msgPrivacyParameters. Encryption uses AES/CFB/NoPadding (128-bit feedback), a stream mode, so ciphertext and plaintext share the same length.

The localized key handed to these methods is the same Kul produced by UsmSecurity.localizeKey(com.nexuslink.protocol.snmp.UsmSecurity.AuthProtocol, byte[], byte[])/UsmSecurity.passwordToLocalizedKey(com.nexuslink.protocol.snmp.UsmSecurity.AuthProtocol, java.lang.String, byte[]); per RFC 3414 §2.6 a distinct privacy passphrase is localized exactly as an auth passphrase is, so no key derivation is re-implemented here.

  • Method Details

    • desEncrypt

      public static UsmPrivacy.Encrypted desEncrypt(byte[] localizedKey, int engineBoots, int localInt, byte[] plaintext)
      Encrypts plaintext with DES-CBC per RFC 3414 §8.1. The salt placed in msgPrivacyParameters is engineBoots || localInt (each 4 octets, big-endian); the CBC IV is pre-IV XOR salt. The plaintext is zero-padded up to a multiple of the 8-octet block (the RFC leaves the pad value irrelevant since the enclosed scopedPDU is self-delimiting), so the ciphertext length is the input length rounded up to the next multiple of 8.
      Parameters:
      localizedKey - the privacy-localized key Kul; at least 16 octets are used
      engineBoots - the authoritative engine's boot counter (high half of the salt)
      localInt - a per-message local integer (low half of the salt)
      plaintext - the data to encrypt (the serialized scopedPDU)
      Returns:
      the ciphertext and the 8-octet salt to advertise as msgPrivacyParameters
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a required argument is null or the key is too short

    • desDecrypt

      public static byte[] desDecrypt(byte[] localizedKey, byte[] privParameters, byte[] ciphertext)
      Inverse of desEncrypt(byte[], int, int, byte[]): decrypts ciphertext using the shared localizedKey and the privParameters (salt) that arrived with the message. The returned buffer still carries any trailing pad octets added at encryption time — the enclosed scopedPDU's own length fields delimit the real payload.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if an argument is null, the key is too short, the salt is not 8 octets, or the ciphertext length is not a multiple of the block

    • aesEncrypt

      public static UsmPrivacy.Encrypted aesEncrypt(byte[] localizedKey, int engineBoots, int engineTime, long salt, byte[] plaintext)
      Encrypts plaintext with AES-128 in CFB mode per RFC 3826. The first 16 octets of localizedKey form the AES key; the 128-bit IV is engineBoots(4) || engineTime(4) || salt(8). CFB is a stream mode, so no padding is applied and the ciphertext has exactly the plaintext length.
      Parameters:
      localizedKey - the privacy-localized key Kul; the first 16 octets are the AES key
      engineBoots - the authoritative engine's boot counter (IV octets 0–3)
      engineTime - the authoritative engine's time (IV octets 4–7)
      salt - a 64-bit per-message salt (IV octets 8–15), advertised as msgPrivacyParameters
      plaintext - the data to encrypt (the serialized scopedPDU)
      Returns:
      the ciphertext and the 8-octet salt to advertise as msgPrivacyParameters
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if a required argument is null or the key is too short

    • aesDecrypt

      public static byte[] aesDecrypt(byte[] localizedKey, int engineBoots, int engineTime, byte[] privParameters, byte[] ciphertext)
